query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine learning assisted high-throughput screening approach, which integrates simulation and experimental data, can rapidly identify refractory HEA compositions that are intrinsically strong, ductile, and low in weight.
generation.material_initial_state: A multi‐principal element refractory alloy system with a vast composition space that has not yet been optimized using traditional thermo‐kinetic and simulation methods.
generation.intervention: Develop and apply a data-driven machine learning model trained on combined simulation and experimental datasets to predict optimal alloy compositions under realistic processing parameters.
generation.conditions: High-throughput screening under practical processing conditions that mimic real-world fabrication (e.g., considered temperature regimes, compositional ranges, and processing rates) for refractory HEAs.
generation.structural_mediator: Optimized element ratios and corresponding phase stability mediated by the predicted lattice distortions and microstructural configurations.
generation.mechanism: The machine learning model identifies nonlinear correlations between composition, microstructural features (such as lattice distortion and phase balance), and mechanical properties. This enables rapid screening of the vast composition space to pinpoint alloys that break the typical strength-ductility trade-off while also reducing weight.
generation.predicted_outcome: Design of a set of refractory HEA compositions exhibiting significantly improved mechanical properties (higher intrinsic strength and ductility) alongside lower density compared to alloys designed via traditional methods.
generation.baseline: Traditional approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and brute-force simulations, which are too time-consuming to efficiently explore the HEA composition space.
generation.boundary: The model’s predictions are reliable only within the compositional and processing parameter ranges represented in the training data. Extrapolation to unrepresented regimes may yield uncertain results.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvements (in terms of strength, ductility and weight reduction percentages) are not fully determined until experimental validation, and potential biases in training data could limit prediction accuracy.

falsification_experiment.design: Use the trained machine learning model to screen and select a series of refractory HEA compositions predicted to be intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight. Fabricate these alloys using realistic processing protocols and compare their mechanical properties and densities with alloys designed using traditional methods.
measurements: Ductility (percent elongation or strain to failure)
Microstructural characterization (e.g., phase identification, lattice distortion)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the fabricated alloys do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in strength and ductility while also achieving lower weight than alloys designed through conventional approaches (at a p-value < 0.05), then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

The computational software could significantly affect the efficiency of HTC since massive calculations are carried out. In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. Metallic alloys containing multiple principal alloying elements, which are known as high-entropy alloys (HEAs) [1] – [3] , have attracted extensive research interest in recent years with many studies focused on their microstructure, mechanical properties, and underlying deformation mechanisms [4] – [6] . For example, as a new class of structural materials, certain face-centered cubic ( fcc ) alloys, in particular CrCoNi-based HEAs, have been shown to possess improved strength and exceptional damage tolerance, especially at cryogenic temperatures [7] , [8] .

A second prominent class of HEA systems are refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), which comprise mostly refractory elements and invariably crystallize as body-centered cubic ( bcc ) solid solutions; these alloys have been considered as promising candidate materials for elevated-temperature applications due to their exceptional resistance to softening and extremely high melting points [9] – [11] .
